question: Which filesystem policy contract should OpenClaw support for host filesystem tools, local media, apply_patch, spawned runs, and shell-mediated exec access?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the solution creates a public config surface and security boundary where naming, deny precedence, normalization, upgrade behavior, and exec scope require maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a versioned tools.fs policy
options.body: Define one canonical allow/deny or roots contract, require normalized deny-wins enforcement across file/media/apply_patch surfaces, and document or separately track the exec boundary.

options.title: Limit v1 to workspaceOnly hardening
options.body: Keep this issue open but defer multi-root allow/deny config until the default workspace boundary and exec story are stronger.

options.title: Defer to sandbox backends
options.body: Reject path ACLs for now and direct users to Docker, SSH, or local-user sandbox isolation as the supported hard boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve a versioned tools.fs policy
recommendation.body: Define one canonical allow/deny or roots contract, require normalized deny-wins enforcement across file/media/apply_patch surfaces, and document or separately track the exec boundary.
